newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Seven says well placed for future.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Seven says well placed for future.

text.p: Seven Network Ltd said on Wednesday it is well-placed for future development following a number of developments in the group's operations over the past six months.

"Seven is well-placed for future development following a number of significant developments in the company's business over the past six months," chairman Kerry Stokes said in a statement accompanying the results for the half year.
Seven reported a 3.2 percent rise in operating profit to A$96 million for the first half of the 1996/97 year, which was well within market expectations.

Seven said the results did not include its interest in Hollywood studio Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer (MGM), which it invested US$250 million last year to take contol of the studio along with U.S. investor Kirk Kerkorian.
The network said the operating profit for the half was a record and was achieved despite a softening in the advertising market during the period.

It said its coverage of the Atlanta Olympics last year produced a small gross profit. It said it recorded an abnormal gain of A$3.2 million on the sale of radio assets of Sunshine Broadcasting, acquired by Seven in December 1995.
Seven, which is 15 percent owned by News Corp Ltd, also declared a half year dividend of 4.5 cents, steady with the same period a year earlier and in line with market expectations.
It said although it does not expect to pay tax for another two years, accounting standards required recognition of this income tax expense.

Seven, which is about 20 percent owned by its chairman Kerry Stokes, reported a net profit of A$62.98 million for the half, compared with A$91.88 million a year earlier. The fall is mainly due to accounting for income tax expense.
At 11.35 a.m. (0035 GMT), Seven shares were three cents lower at A$4.10.
